principles: A word that costs someone money

world_behind.title: The objection is financial
world_behind.text: Verse 3 says the popular part of the Zoramites was angry because the preaching destroyed their craft. Mormon puts the motive in one clause and does not elaborate.

world_behind.title: The leaders polled the people secretly
world_behind.text: Verse 5 says the rulers, priests, and teachers hid their own intentions and found out the minds of the people privily. The expulsion in verse 6 follows a covert survey.

world_behind.title: Everyone who agreed was expelled
world_behind.text: Verse 6 says they were many. The poor of Alma 32 were shut out of buildings; now anyone persuaded is put out of the country.

world_behind.title: The people of Ammon are threatened for taking them in
world_behind.text: Verses 8 and 9 have the Zoramite chief ruler demand they be cast out, and breathe out threatenings. The people of Ammon refuse and receive the refugees anyway.

world_behind.title: They give land, not only shelter
world_behind.text: Verse 9 lists nourishing, clothing, lands for inheritance, and ministering according to their wants. Alma 27 had them receiving exactly this from the Nephites.

world_behind.title: Jershon is vacated for an army
world_behind.text: Verse 13 has the people of Ammon move to Melek so the land can become a staging ground. They give up an inheritance to keep the covenant of Alma 24 intact.

world_behind.title: The converts take up arms
world_behind.text: Verse 14 says the Zoramites brought to repentance now defend themselves, their wives, children, and lands. Their neighbors in Jershon had buried their weapons.

words.text: A trade, and the income from it. The record uses the word twice and the King James Bible six times; Acts 19 has a silversmith telling his guild that by this craft they have their wealth, just before a riot against Paul. Mormon uses it for the same kind of objection.

Secretly, without being noticed. The record uses it four times and the King James Bible fifteen. Here the leaders learn the people's minds without letting the people learn theirs, which turns a consultation into an intelligence operation.

Threats, stated to intimidate. The record uses it ten times and the King James Bible twice, one of which is Saul breathing out threatenings against the disciples. Mormon uses the same verb, and the people of Ammon are unmoved by it.

Between. The record uses it five times and the King James Bible sixteen. Mormon uses it to date the start of the war in the eighteenth year, and to say that the fighting begins in the land the people of Ammon just vacated.

Rigor, exactness in requirement. The word occurs twice in this record and never in the King James Bible. Jacob 2 has hearts pierced by the strictness of the word; here people are offended by it, and Mormon names it as what turned them hard.

An instruction laid on someone as a duty. The record uses it ten times and the King James Bible a hundred and two. Benjamin gave Mosiah charge over the kingdom; Alma gives each son his own, separately, and Alma 36 through 42 are the text of them.

phrases.term: They were angry because of the word, for it did destroy their craft
phrases.text: Mormon supplies the motive before the response. The preaching threatened a livelihood, and the anger that follows is presented as an economic reaction dressed as a religious one.

phrases.term: Their rulers and their priests and their teachers did not let the people know concerning their desires
phrases.text: The leadership consults while concealing its own position. Mormon notes the asymmetry, and verse 6 shows what it was for: identifying who to expel.

phrases.term: Those who were in favor of the words which had been spoken by Alma and his brethren were cast out of the land; and they were many
phrases.text: The last clause is the sting. The mission worked, and the measure of its success is the size of the refugee column moving toward Jershon.

phrases.term: He breathed out many threatenings against them
phrases.text: The Zoramite ruler's demand, in language the King James Bible uses of Saul before Damascus. Mormon reports the threat and the refusal in the same verse.

phrases.term: They did receive all the poor of the Zoramites that came over unto them
phrases.text: The people of Ammon take in a whole displaced population under threat of war. Alma 27 had them arriving in Jershon as refugees themselves, and Mormon lets the reader make the connection.

phrases.term: They did nourish them, and did clothe them, and did give unto them lands for their inheritance
phrases.text: Three verbs and a grant of property. The clothing is pointed: Alma 32 said these people were excluded over the coarseness of their apparel.

phrases.term: Gave place in the land of Jershon for the armies of the Nephites
phrases.text: The people of Ammon hand over the land they were granted so it can become a battlefield. Their covenant keeps them out of the fighting, so they move instead of staying to be defended in place.

phrases.term: They have taken up arms to defend themselves, and their wives, and children, and their lands
phrases.text: The Zoramite converts make the opposite decision from their hosts. Mormon records both choices without ranking them, and the two peoples live in the same story.

phrases.term: They began to be offended because of the strictness of the word
phrases.text: Alma's grief in Zarahemla has a stated cause. The word had not softened and the people had, and Mormon says the offense was at the strictness itself.

phrases.term: That he might give unto them every one his charge, separately
phrases.text: Alma gathers three sons and speaks to each alone. The separateness is recorded deliberately, and the next seven chapters are what he said.

verses.label: v. 1–2
verses.title: Withdrawal
verses.text: Amulek finishes and the company withdraws from the multitude into Jershon. The rest of the brethren finish preaching to the Zoramites and follow.

verses.label: v. 3–7
verses.title: The poll and the expulsion
verses.text: The popular part of the Zoramites is angry because the word destroys their craft. Their rulers, priests, and teachers gather the people, conceal their own aims, and learn the people's minds secretly. Everyone in favor is cast out, and there are many. Alma and his brethren minister to them in Jershon.

verses.label: v. 8–9
verses.title: The threat, and the reception
verses.text: The Zoramite chief ruler demands the people of Ammon expel the refugees and breathes out threatenings. They are unafraid, keep them, and nourish, clothe, grant land, and minister according to their wants.

verses.label: v. 10–12
verses.title: War
verses.text: The Zoramites are angered and go to the Lamanites to stir them up. Both prepare for war against the people of Ammon and the Nephites. The seventeenth year of the judges ends.

verses.label: v. 13–14
verses.title: Jershon vacated
verses.text: The people of Ammon move to Melek and give the land over to the Nephite armies. War begins in the eighteenth year. Alma, Ammon, their brethren, and Alma's two sons return to Zarahemla, having brought many Zoramites to repentance; those converts now hold land in Jershon and have taken up arms.

verses.label: v. 15–16
verses.title: Alma's grief, and the charges
verses.text: He is grieved for the iniquity, the wars, the bloodsheds, and the contentions, and for a people growing hard and offended at the strictness of the word. He gathers his sons and gives each his charge separately, and the record of those charges follows.

chapter.title: The mission succeeded and produced a refugee crisis
chapter.text: Many believed, and all of them lost their homes. Mormon reports the conversion count and the expulsion in the same sentence.

chapter.title: Money is named as the reason for the anger
chapter.text: Verse 3 says the word destroyed their craft. Everything the Zoramites do afterward follows from a threat to income, and the record says so plainly.

chapter.title: The consultation was a screening
chapter.text: Leaders who hid their own intentions asked everyone else theirs. Mormon describes a process that looks participatory and functions as a purge.

chapter.title: Refugees receive refugees
chapter.text: The people of Ammon had arrived in Jershon with nothing eleven years earlier. They now give land, clothing, and food to a second displaced people, under threat.

chapter.title: They give up the land rather than the covenant
chapter.text: Jershon was granted to them and they hand it back so an army can use it. The cost of keeping their oath in Alma 24 is paid here in property.

chapter.title: Two converted peoples make opposite choices about arms
chapter.text: The people of Ammon will not fight; the Zoramite converts take up arms for their families and lands. Mormon puts both in one chapter and passes no judgment.

chapter.title: Offense at strictness is the diagnosis for Zarahemla
chapter.text: Alma's sorrow is not about a foreign nation. His own people are hardening, and what they object to is the exactness of what he has been preaching.

chapter.title: The chapter ends by turning private
chapter.text: After war preparations and national movements, Mormon closes on a father gathering three sons and speaking to each alone. The next seven chapters are that conversation.

applications.title: Look for the money behind the objection
applications.text: The Zoramite leaders were angry because the preaching cost them income. When someone resists an idea hard, ask what it would cost them if they accepted it.

applications.title: Say what you want before you ask what they want
applications.text: The leaders concealed their aims and collected everyone else's. When you are gathering opinions, put your own position on the table first.

applications.title: Receive people who are costing you something
applications.text: The people of Ammon took in refugees while being threatened with war. When helping someone would make your own position worse, that is the moment the help counts.

applications.title: Give the charge separately
applications.text: Alma spoke to each son alone instead of lecturing all three. When you have something important to say to several people, work out what each of them specifically needs to hear.

questions.text: What would I lose if the thing I resist turned out to be true?
When have I asked for input while hiding what I had already decided?
What has agreeing with something true cost me?
Who has arrived in my life needing something, and what did I actually give?
What would I hand over to keep a promise I made?
Where have I been offended by the strictness of something rather than its truth?
Who needs to hear from me alone, and about what?
